summary: Chelan County, WA lookout site: an L-4 cab built in 1933 and removed in 1974; a hiker's trip report describes old remains on the summit.

facts.status_note: Cab removed in 1974; a hiker's trip report (undated) describes old remains of a lookout on the summit

access.note: Reached on foot by a trail from the White River; no official access rule in the sources read

visit.trail_note: Hike from the White River: cross the White River on a big bridge, then climb 3000 feet of switchbacks to the ridge (hiker's trip report)

events.note: Lookout was to be stationed on Mount David that week, but the opening was postponed because of snow (Wenatchee Daily World, as quoted by Forest Lookouts)
Magnus Bakke named as Mount David lookout (Leavenworth Echo, June 1933, as quoted by Forest Lookouts)
Cab burned with helicopter help to remove debris (WillhiteWeb)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: WillhiteWeb says panoramic photos were taken in 1974, but its own photo captions read 8-22-1934 and Forest Lookouts dates the panoramas to August 22, 1934. The story uses 1934 and reports the disagreement.

notes_for_editor: Four sources, no Forest Service page for this site. The Forest Lookouts and WillhiteWeb pages carry most of the history. The WillhiteWeb trip report is undated, so the 'old remains' line may be out of date. Firetower.org's cached page shows a 'Date Registered' label with no value, so the 2012 FFLOS registration date in the brief was not verified and is not in the events.
